boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Claremont Village destinations on Yale Avenue, West First Street, and Harvard Avenue, immediately west of Pomona College.

cards.title: Folk Music Center & Museum
cards.subtitle: Yale Avenue corridor • 220 Yale Avenue
cards.notes: Walk Yale Avenue to browse the named Folk Music Center & Museum, then check its official page for current lesson, repair, and appraisal services.
cards.short_summary: A Yale Avenue music destination with documented classes, repairs, and appraisals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Folk Music Center & Museum is located at 220 Yale Avenue and lists classes and lessons, appraisals, and repairs.
cards.access_notes: Check the official site for current hours and service availability.

cards.title: Some Crust Bakery & Cafe
cards.subtitle: Yale Avenue corridor • 119 Yale Avenue
cards.notes: Use the Yale Avenue walk to stop at Some Crust Bakery & Cafe; the Village directory identifies the cafe by name and street address.
cards.short_summary: A named bakery and cafe directly on the Yale Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village's official shop-and-dine directory lists Some Crust Bakery & Cafe at 119 Yale Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; confirm current service details with the business.

cards.title: Hens' Kitchen Shoppe
cards.subtitle: Yale Avenue corridor • 141 Yale Avenue
cards.notes: Pause along Yale Avenue to browse Hens' Kitchen Shoppe, a specifically listed kitchen-goods destination rather than an unnamed storefront.
cards.short_summary: A named kitchen shop on the Yale Avenue commercial corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village's official directory lists Hens' Kitchen Shoppe at 141 Yale Avenue under gifts and specialty shopping.
cards.access_notes: Retail items require purchase; verify current hours before making a special trip.

cards.title: Claremont Lewis Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 200 W. First Street, at the Claremont Depot
cards.notes: Walk West First Street to the museum entrance on the Depot's north side; Pomona students can enter without admission under the museum's student policy.
cards.short_summary: A First Street art museum in the historic Claremont Depot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Lewis Museum of Art is at 200 W. First Street in the Claremont Depot; students receive free general admission.
cards.source_title: Claremont Lewis Museum of Art — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Students are free; bring student identification and check the museum's current public hours.

cards.title: Claremont Depot
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 200 W. First Street
cards.notes: Use the historic Depot as a West First Street landmark: its north side faces First Street and houses the Claremont Lewis Museum of Art entrance.
cards.short_summary: A named historic depot anchoring the First Street edge of the Village.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Lewis Museum of Art states that it is in the Claremont Depot at 200 W. First Street, with its entrance facing First Street.
cards.source_title: Claremont Lewis Museum of Art — Plan Your Visit
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing does not require admission; museum access follows its published hours.

cards.title: Claremont Packing House
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 532 W. First Street
cards.notes: Continue west on First Street to see the 1922 Packing House and choose among its documented shops, restaurants, arts, and classes.
cards.short_summary: A preserved former citrus packing house repurposed for Village retail and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Packing House at 532 W. First Street is a historic Village landmark with shops, restaurants, arts, and classes.
cards.access_notes: Individual tenants and activities may have separate hours and charges.

cards.title: Forum Bookshop
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 586 W. First Street
cards.notes: Follow West First Street to Forum Bookshop to browse books, cards, bookmarks, and journals; purchases support the Prison Library Project.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit-linked bookshop whose sales support a books-to-prisoners program.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Forum identifies its bookshop at 586 W. First Street and says purchases support the Prison Library Project.
cards.access_notes: Browsing is available during the bookshop's posted hours; merchandise requires purchase.

cards.title: JAX Bicycle Center
cards.subtitle: West First Street corridor • 217 W. First Street
cards.notes: On the West First Street corridor, use JAX Bicycle Center as a named stop for bicycle-related retail or service needs before heading farther into the Village.
cards.short_summary: A specifically listed bicycle shop on West First Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village's official directory lists JAX Bicycle Center at 217 W. First Street.
cards.access_notes: Retail goods and shop services require purchase; confirm current service availability directly.

cards.title: Boon Companion Toys
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue corridor • 145 Harvard Avenue
cards.notes: Turn onto Harvard Avenue for Boon Companion Toys, a named specialty retail stop listed at 145 Harvard Avenue in the Village directory.
cards.short_summary: A named toy store on the Harvard Avenue portion of Claremont Village.
cards.evidence_claim: Claremont Village's official directory lists Boon Companion Toys at 145 Harvard Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Retail items require purchase; verify current opening details with the shop.

cards.title: Claremont Farmers & Artisans Market
cards.subtitle: Harvard Avenue corridor • Claremont Village
cards.notes: Plan a Sunday Harvard Avenue walk around the Farmers & Artisans Market, where the Forum documents fresh produce, local farms, and handcrafted goods.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Sunday market on Harvard Avenue in Claremont Village.
cards.evidence_claim: The Claremont Forum states that its Farmers & Artisans Market operates Sundays from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Harvard Avenue in Claremont Village.
cards.access_notes: The market is documented for Sundays, 8 a.m.–1 p.m.; vendors' goods are individually priced.
